standard_prerequisites: The comparison of the small Zariski and etale sites and the sheaf property of the associated etale structure sheaf from Descent
The equivalence of quasi-coherent modules on the small etale site with quasi-coherent modules on X, from Descent
Vanishing of higher cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves on affine objects, and the site-level lemma expressing cohomology over U through the top cohomology sheaf
core_obligations: Show R epsilon_* restricts to a functor on derived categories of quasi-coherent modules by computing its cohomology sheaves as epsilon_* of the cohomology sheaves of the input
Prove the unit adjunction is an isomorphism for quasi-coherent modules and, using the module-level equivalence, also the counit
For E in the derived etale category, compute H^q(U, E) = H^0(U, H^q(E)) over affine objects and sheafify to get H^q(R epsilon_* E) = epsilon_* H^q(E)
Conclude both adjunction maps are isomorphisms using exactness of epsilon^*
proof_roadmap: Set up the adjunction between epsilon^* and R epsilon_* and reduce to cohomology sheaf comparisons
Handle modules first: unit and counit isomorphisms from the Descent equivalence
Compute the cohomology sheaves of R epsilon_* E over affines via the cohomology-over-U lemma
Sheafify, transport through epsilon^*, and close both directions of the equivalence
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the equivalence of the derived category of quasi-coherent modules on a scheme with that on its small etale site via epsilon^* (source lines 401-470, label lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site). The solver must assemble the quasi-inverse on the derived level from module-level data: compute cohomology sheaves of the pushforward through an affine-vanishing argument, sheafify, and verify both adjunction maps; the derived-level bookkeeping across the two topologies is not a routine citation. Allowed background: the Descent equivalences and cohomology lemmas cited, delivered as navigation pointers.
